newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Reliance outlines bright future.
newsitem.headline: India's Reliance outlines bright future.

text.p: Petrochemicals giant Reliance Industries on Thursday offered investors a generous bonus equity issue and forecast a rosy future with sales nearing 200 billion rupees ($5.5 billion) by 2000.
Sales in the year ended March 31 totalled 87.3 billion rupees, up from 77.86 billion in 1995/96 (April-March).
Company chairman Dhirubhai Ambani ended weeks of feverish stock market guessing when he announced a one-for-one bonus share issue at a packed annual shareholders meeting.
"A bonus offer reflects our confidence in the future earnings growth of the company," Ambani said.

Reliance shares -- which have surged some 85 percent on the Bombay bourse this calendar year -- leapt to a new 52-week high of 388 rupees. Profit taking near close erased some gains and the shares ended 11.0 rupees up at 377.50.
Reliance began life as a commodities trading firm in 1958, and under the control of the Ambani family built itself into India's largest private sector company.
"We do not foresee any further equity dilution over the next two to three years, excluding outstanding conversions (of debentures)," Ambani told shareholders.
He said he favoured a share buy back programme and would examine this option as soon as a new Companies Act became law.
Ambani said the firm recognised the need to improve capital efficiency as measured by return on equity and earnings growth.
"We have set ourselves the targets of achieving a 20 percent compounded growth in earnings per share and a return of 20 percent of shareholders funds over the next five years."
Petrochemicals analysts said the projections were above their estimates.
"Ambani has made a lot of promises which people will like," said an analyst at a leading U.S. brokerage.

"He's projected an earnings growth of 20 percent, talked about buy back and no equity dilution -- all these are positive things," he said, adding that he expected earnings to grow at a more modest 17.5 percent.

In a recent joint report on Reliance, Goldman Sachs and its Indian affiliate Kotak Securities said the increased burden of finance charges due to the firm's aggressive expansion plans and falling margins in petrochemicals will hit earnings growth.
Earnings per share was likely to grow by 10.6 percent in the current 1997/98 financial year, and would fall by 6.2 percent in 1998/99, the report said.

"The company has cash flows sufficient for projects they have in mind and they can manage with debt till 1998/98," said Kotak analyst Sanjeev Prasad, reacting to Ambani's statement on no immediate equity dilutions.
Prasad said he was maintaining his earnings forecasts for the time being.
Analysts said the robust earnings projects were unlikely to translate into a stock price outperformance.
"Today's bonus news will be good for sentiment but the stock has gone up quite a bit and we expect the price to stabilise in this range in the coming months," said the analyst at the U.S. brokerage.
--Bombay Newsroom (91) 22 265 9000
